values: Pilot an evidence-linked financial research report for one Indian IPO. Keep the underlying financial schema reusable for listed companies.
Ratio displays and company research already exist. Auditability and measured extraction quality are a defensible learning objective.
Choose a pilot and map the evidence needed for one complete report.
Close alternatives already claim RHP extraction, source-page traces, scoring and valuation. Choose an improvement that can be measured.
Evidence links alone are not a supported novelty claim. Extraction accuracy, historical reproducibility or sector-specific analysis may offer room to improve.
Compare one shared RHP across the closest tools. Interview 3 potential users.
Begin with transparent ratio trends and a separately explained rule-based baseline.
F-score provides a concrete reference but is not an Indian IPO distress probability. Missing data must stay missing.
Read original definitions and assess whether each signal fits an IPO issuer.
Show a peer-based range and sensitivity to peer selection. Keep listing return a separate outcome.
Published findings differ with method. One multiple or one peer set should not create false precision.
Read both IPO valuation papers fully and draft inclusion/exclusion rules.
Verify one company and a few peers manually before scaling extraction.
Filing metadata, document dates, units and statement basis require explicit reconciliation.
Confirm canonical pre-offer RHP and extract a small labelled table.
Evaluate fact extraction, evidence retrieval and arithmetic separately. Add narrative generation after numerical checks.
A plausible answer can contain the wrong source, period or calculation.
Create 20–30 manually answered questions, including missing/ambiguous cases.
Label reports created now from old documents as retrospective reconstructions.
Assessment date, disclosure availability and later revisions affect what could have been known.
Define as-of date, document version, peer-price date and separate later outcomes.
Defer revenue forecasts and calibrated distress probabilities until targets, labelled data and validation are defined.
Three example issuers can support a pilot, not supervised-model validation across IPOs.
Define a measurable target before collecting a larger chronological cohort.
Method comparison for F-score and IPO peer valuation
Definitions and competing assumptions recorded from full texts.
Canonical pre-offer document and 15–20 fields verified with source pages.
Audit closest GitHub projects and products
Trace one real issuer from source to output. Record licenses, tests and unverified claims.
Manually labelled table and error taxonomy
Same pages tested for headers, units, signs, periods and footnotes.
Gold questions and chronological validation plan
Answer, arithmetic, evidence and as-of-date checks specified.
This is a first-pass discovery survey. Abstract, excerpt and selected-section reviews are explicitly identified. No product account, parser or agent was run.
Source observations are in column G of Survey log. Learnings and proposed uses are interpretations, not claims made by the source.
Filter the survey by type or review depth. Update the review depth and next step as the team reads or tests each source. A blank year means no publication year was established.
Coverage gaps: Indian empirical validation, Altman/Ohlson/Beneish model suitability, accounting definitions, historical pricing access, legal/data-reuse terms and user demand. These remain open.

values: Value Investing: The Use of Historical Financial Statement Information to Separate Winners from Losers
Joseph D. Piotroski. Journal of Accounting Research 38, supplement, 1–41.
Nine binary signals cover profitability, leverage/liquidity and operating efficiency. F-score sums these signals.
Read abstract and financial-signal methodology, PDF pp. 7–10.
Simple accounting rules offer an explainable baseline.
Test original F-score alongside separate ratio trends. Publish every component and missing input.
Original population differs from Indian IPO issuers. An IPO share issue can affect the equity-issuance signal. Score is not a calibrated distress probability.
Open paper PDF hosted by Ivey.
Read precise denominator and equity-issuance definitions before implementation.
Amiyatosh K. Purnanandam and Bhaskaran Swaminathan. Review of Financial Studies 17(3), 811–848. DOI 10.1093/rfs/hhg055.
Publisher abstract reports offer-price overvaluation of 14%–50%, depending on peer matching, despite positive first-day returns.
Compare offer valuation with industry peer multiples. Abstract reviewed.
Listing gains and relative fundamental valuation answer different questions.
Separate valuation range from listing-return outcome. Vary peer matching and show the sensitivity.
US historical evidence is not a result about Indian IPOs. Estimates depend on peer criteria. Full methods not reviewed.
Abstract open. Publisher full text may require access.
Read full method with R03 and reproduce alternative matching rules on a small Indian sample.
Steven X. Zheng. Journal of Empirical Finance 14(3), 287–309. DOI 10.1016/j.jempfin.2006.06.001.
Publisher search excerpt challenges earlier overpricing conclusions using a modified valuation method.
Publisher excerpt only. Direct publisher page returned 403.
Competing findings make model specification a research question.
Compare more than one peer-selection and aggregation rule before declaring an IPO expensive.
Full paper not reviewed. Do not treat this as a settled rebuttal or transfer its findings directly to India.
Publisher page blocked in this browser. Locate an author manuscript or library copy.
Obtain full text and document exactly which corrections change the earlier findings.
FinQA: A Dataset of Numerical Reasoning over Financial Data
Zhiyu Chen et al. EMNLP 2021. arXiv:2109.00122.
Financial reports and numerical question answering
Expert-written questions include gold reasoning programs for explainability. Paper describes gaps between models and experts.
Abstract and linked repository overview reviewed.
A correct answer needs a defensible computation path.
Store operands, source locations, formula and result. Build local questions for margins, growth and cash conversion.
Not an Indian IPO dataset. Benchmark results do not establish performance on Indian prospectuses.
Open paper and public code/data repository. Dataset terms need separate review.
Read dataset schema and adapt 10–20 question patterns to manually verified prospectus facts.
TAT-QA: A Question Answering Benchmark on a Hybrid of Tabular and Textual Content in Finance
Fengbin Zhu et al. ACL 2021. arXiv:2105.07624.
Financial reports combining tables and narrative
TAGOP selects relevant table cells and text spans, then applies symbolic operations.
Table cells alone may omit units, footnotes and definitions.
Preserve table headers, adjacent notes, period, currency unit and consolidation basis during extraction.
Benchmark data and models are not validated for Indian offer documents. Full experimental method not reviewed.
Open paper. Follow paper links for dataset and terms.
Inspect examples involving units, signs and table-to-text reasoning.
FinanceBench: A New Benchmark for Financial Question Answering
Open-book QA over publicly traded companies
Describes 10,231 questions with answers and evidence. Evaluates 16 model configurations on 150 cases.
Abstract reviewed. Public dataset link followed.
Evidence retrieval and correct answering need separate evaluation.
Measure answer accuracy and evidence correctness on a local gold set. Include unanswerable questions.
2023 model performance is historical. The public sample is not the entire question collection. Indian document accuracy remains untested.
Open paper and public sample. Check dataset card before reuse.
Read scoring protocol and design a small Indian IPO evaluation set.

Tianyu Zhou, Pinqiao Wang, Yilin Wu and Hongyang Yang. arXiv:2411.08804.
Presents an agent-based equity-research approach with quantitative analysis and valuation.
